title: Centre Tank Boost Pump — Removal

issue.reason: Original issue of the centre tank boost pump removal task.

abstract: Removal of a centre tank boost pump with its inlet screen, including the tank entry precautions and the debris recovery step that has to be completed before the pump leaves the tank.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of one centre tank boost pump, its screen carrier and its inlet screen, and the recovery of any debris found at the pump inlet.
sections.job_setup_note: The centre tank must be defuelled, drained, purged and confirmed gas-free before entry, and the gas-free reading must be repeated every thirty minutes while a person is inside. A second person must remain at the access panel with the recovery harness for the whole time. Only non-sparking tools may be taken into the tank and every item taken in must be logged on the tool control card.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE FUEL TANK UNTIL IT IS CONFIRMED GAS-FREE AND A SECOND PERSON IS AT THE ACCESS PANEL WITH THE RECOVERY HARNESS. 2. Defuel, drain and purge the centre tank to the standard practice. 3. Confirm the gas-free reading and record it. 4. Open the wing tank access panels and log every tool taken into the tank. 5. Disconnect the electrical connector at the pump and fit the blanking cap. 6. CAUTION: USE NON-SPARKING TOOLS ONLY INSIDE THE TANK. A SPARK IN A PURGED TANK IS STILL A HAZARD. 7. Release the pump inlet actuator D2820111798703 from its mounting and support it while the last fastener is removed. 8. Withdraw the pump and the screen carrier together and put them on the tank entry mat. 9. Recover every fragment found in the screen and at the pump inlet and put them in the sample bag. 10. Clean the screen with aviation grade cleaning solvent and the soft brush from the kit, working from the clean face outwards, and dry it with filtered air. 11. Examine the inlet manifold CIN652579-17 for further debris and record what is found. 12. Fit the tank blank to the pump aperture. 13. Remove the tool control card items from the tank and confirm the count.
sections.close_out: Confirm the tool count against the tool control card before the access panel is closed or the tank is left unattended. Fit the tank blank if the installation will not follow immediately. Record the gas-free readings, the debris recovered and the pump serial number in the aircraft technical record.

safety_precautions: Do not enter the tank until the gas-free reading is confirmed.
Keep a second person at the access panel with the recovery harness.
Use non-sparking tools only inside the tank.

title: Centre Tank Boost Pump — Removal

issue.reason: Screen cleaning solvent replaced by the mild alkaline cleaner, because the previous solvent attacks the coating on the coarse mesh screen.

abstract: Removal of a centre tank boost pump with its inlet screen, including the tank entry precautions, the debris recovery step and the screen cleaning method that both screen standards tolerate.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of one centre tank boost pump, its screen carrier and its inlet screen, and the recovery of any debris found at the pump inlet.
sections.job_setup_note: The centre tank must be defuelled, drained, purged and confirmed gas-free before entry, and the gas-free reading must be repeated every thirty minutes while a person is inside. A second person must remain at the access panel with the recovery harness for the whole time. Only non-sparking tools may be taken into the tank and every item taken in must be logged on the tool control card. Take the mild alkaline cleaner and the demineralised water into the tank with the tool kit: the aviation grade solvent that used to be used for the screen is no longer acceptable on either screen standard and must not be carried in for this task.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE FUEL TANK UNTIL IT IS CONFIRMED GAS-FREE AND A SECOND PERSON IS AT THE ACCESS PANEL WITH THE RECOVERY HARNESS. 2. Defuel, drain and purge the centre tank to the standard practice. 3. Confirm the gas-free reading and record it. 4. Open the wing tank access panels and log every tool taken into the tank. 5. Disconnect the electrical connector at the pump and fit the blanking cap. 6. CAUTION: USE NON-SPARKING TOOLS ONLY INSIDE THE TANK. A SPARK IN A PURGED TANK IS STILL A HAZARD. 7. Release the pump inlet actuator D2820111798703 from its mounting and support it while the last fastener is removed. 8. Withdraw the pump and the screen carrier together and put them on the tank entry mat. 9. Recover every fragment found in the screen and at the pump inlet and put them in the sample bag. 10. CAUTION: DO NOT CLEAN ANY INLET SCREEN WITH AVIATION GRADE SOLVENT. THE COATING ON THE COARSE MESH SCREEN IS ATTACKED BY IT AND THE DAMAGE IS NOT VISIBLE UNTIL THE SCREEN SHEDS IN SERVICE. 11. Clean the screen with the mild alkaline cleaner and the soft brush from the kit, working from the clean face outwards, rinse with demineralised water and dry with filtered air. 12. Examine the inlet manifold CIN652579-17 for further debris and record what is found. 13. Fit the tank blank to the pump aperture. 14. Remove the tool control card items from the tank and confirm the count.
sections.close_out: Confirm the tool count against the tool control card before the access panel is closed or the tank is left unattended. Fit the tank blank if the installation will not follow immediately. Record the gas-free readings, the debris recovered and the pump serial number in the aircraft technical record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. On aircraft at the coarse mesh screen standard the screen is recovered for inspection but not returned.

safety_precautions: Do not enter the tank until the gas-free reading is confirmed.
Keep a second person at the access panel with the recovery harness.
Use non-sparking tools only inside the tank.
